question: Is it changing, where, and is something unusual happening?

cdc2001.cite: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (2001). Updated guidelines for evaluating public health surveillance systems. Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, Recommendations and Reports.
cdc2001.checked: every quote read word for word on the CDC MMWR web page (in Chrome, 20 Nov 2026); the web page has no page numbers, so places are given as its sections and task labels (e.g. D.2.h); in-text reference numbers are left out. The volume and issue were not read on the page and are not given. The card's own reference (Thacker & Berkelman 1988) is not open access and was not read

steps.title: Define a case
steps.text: Write down exactly what counts as a case: symptoms, test results, place and time, and how certain each level is.

quotes.text: A public health surveillance system is dependent on a clear case definition for the health-related event under surveillance

steps.title: Collect, always
steps.text: Gather the same data the same way, week after week and place by place, for as long as the system runs.

quotes.text: Public health surveillance is the ongoing, systematic collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination of data regarding a health-related event for use in public health action to reduce morbidity and mortality and to improve health

steps.title: Report fast
steps.text: Data flow from the people who see cases to those who can act. Every step between them takes time, and the delays can be measured.

quotes.text: Timeliness reflects the speed between steps in a public health surveillance system.

steps.title: Spot the signal
steps.text: Compare the latest counts with the usual level for that place and season. A rise beyond it is a signal to investigate, not yet a cause.

quotes.text: detect trends that signal changes in the occurrence of disease, injury, or adverse or protective exposure, including detection of epidemics (or outbreaks)

steps.title: Know what's missed
steps.text: No system catches every case. A trend can still be trusted if the share caught stays the same; a change in reporting can look like a change in disease.

quotes.text: A public health surveillance system that does not have high sensitivity can still be useful in monitoring trends as long as the sensitivity remains reasonably constant over time.

selection-bias.text: A public health surveillance system that is representative accurately describes the occurrence of a health-related event over time and its distribution in the population by place and person.

limits: The page follows the CDC's 2001 evaluation guidelines, not the card's reference (Thacker & Berkelman 1988), which was not read.
The card's examples (the Mauna Loa CO₂ record, pharmacovigilance) were not read for this page; no data from them are shown.
The step texts in our own words are summaries of the quotes beside them; the quotes are the authority.
